title: Shadow probe fencing and rollback rate-limiter for staged rollouts
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description:
Goal: Implement a policy component that composes two novel controls for safer staged releases: 1) shadow-probe fencing - a configurable, progressive shadow traffic probing mechanism that exercises a candidate model on a small slice of production requests with strict circuit-breaker style fences (error/latency/quality thresholds) and 2) rollback rate-limiter - a throttling layer that prevents rapid flip-flop rollbacks by enforcing cooldown windows, exponential backoff on automated rollbacks, and operator-notification escalations.

Rationale: We frequently see noisy regression signals during early canaries that either (a) trigger automated rollback too aggressively on transient spikes, or (b) allow a bad variant to creep into traffic because shadow probing lacks adequate isolation and gating. Combining a fenced shadow probe with a rollback rate-limiter reduces false positives, reduces human toil, and improves platform stability while preserving fast rollback semantics for genuine incidents.

Design notes:
- Policy model is declarative. Customers (or internal rollout defaults) specify a staging policy object attached to a rollout: {"fence": {...}, "probe": {...}, "rollback": {...}}.
- Fence semantics: configured thresholds for error-rate, p95 latency, and downstream-model-quality delta (via eval hooks). Crossing a fence triggers either: (a) immediate circuit open for the candidate in shadow mode (stop shadowing), (b) escalate to canary pause in staged rollout, or (c) mark for auto-rollback if rollback budget allows.
- Shadow probe progression: percent schedule expressed as discrete steps (0.1%, 1%, 5%) plus probing buckets for different user cohorts. Probes run with mirrored requests and a strict sidecar timeout (shorter than main request TTL) and never return mirrored outputs to users.
- Rollback rate-limiter: parameters: cooldown_window (minutes), rollback_budget (number per 24h), progressive_backoff_factor. When an automated rollback fires, the engine records an event with a TTL; subsequent rollback triggers consult the TTL and may be deferred and sent as a human-review task if within cooldown.
- Safety: allow a forced immediate rollback override by SREs through console (with audit log). Auto-rollback still bypasses cooldown if a critical SLO breach is detected (configurable critical thresholds).

Operational telemetry and SLOs:
- Emit events for fence trips, shadow-fence actions, rollback-decisions, and cooldown-blocks.
- New dashboards: 1) "Fence trips by model" 2) "Shadow probe pass/fail rate" 3) "Rollback frequency and cooldown hits".
- Alerting: critical alert when fence trips > X in Y minutes OR auto-rollback rate exceeds configured budget.

Example policy (YAML snippet):

fence:
  error_rate_threshold: "0.008" # 0.8% on mirrored requests
  p95_latency_ms: "1200"
  quality_delta_threshold: "0.05" # relative BLEU/embedding-sim change
  action_on_trip: "stop_shadow" # choices: stop_shadow | pause_canary | mark_rollback
probe:
  progression_steps: ["0.1%","1%","5%"]
  cohorts: ["internal-beta","canary-users"]
  sidecar_timeout_ms: "500"
rollback:
  cooldown_window_minutes: "30"
  rollback_budget_per_24h: "2"
  backoff_factor: "2"
  critical_thresholds:
    error_rate: "0.05"
    p95_latency_ms: "5000"

Acceptance criteria: 
- Engine accepts declarative policy and persists it to rollout manifest.
- During simulated load tests, fence trips trigger expected actions (stop_shadow or pause) and emit telemetry.
- Rollback rate-limiter prevents second automated rollback within cooldown window and generates an operator task instead.
- Console exposes policy UI to inspect fence history and to force-override cooldown.
- Unit and e2e tests for fence evaluation logic and cooldown state machine.

Backward compatibility: Default behavior when no policy present remains current rollout semantics (existing automated rollback logic unchanged). If a policy is present, policy evaluation is consulted before auto-rollback is enacted.

Risks and tradeoffs:
- Added complexity in rollback path may increase mean time to full rollback for real incidents if thresholds are misconfigured. Mitigation: provide conservative defaults and allow immediate override for SREs.
- Telemetry volume increases from mirrored requests — we will sample mirrored request metrics and cap retention for shadow-specific traces.

Next steps:
1) Design review with SRE/PM/Design (scheduled 2025-02-20).
2) Prototype fence evaluator library (server-side) and integrate with rollout controller.
3) Add UI surfaces in Console for policy authoring and historical fence events.
4) QA run on staging with two customer-facing models, validate that rollback_budget behavior prevents flapping.

Related artifacts: Confluence design doc, prototype server PR, draft Console mockups.
